blueprint_concepts: Conjugate, modulus and argument of a complex number
english: Let $\hat{u}=l\hat{i}+m\hat{j}+n\hat{k}$ be a unit vector which makes an obtuse angle with the positive direction of the $z$-axis. Let $w=l+\mathrm{i}\,m$, where $\mathrm{i}=\sqrt{-1}$, be such that $|w|=\dfrac{3}{5}$ and $(3-4\mathrm{i})\,\overline{w}$ is a negative real number, where $\overline{w}$ denotes the complex conjugate of $w$. Then the value of $l+m+n$ is ______.
hindi: माना $\hat{u}=l\hat{i}+m\hat{j}+n\hat{k}$ एक मात्रक सदिश है जो $z$-अक्ष की धनात्मक दिशा के साथ अधिक कोण बनाता है। माना $w=l+\mathrm{i}\,m$, जहाँ $\mathrm{i}=\sqrt{-1}$ है, इस प्रकार है कि $|w|=\dfrac{3}{5}$ है तथा $(3-4\mathrm{i})\,\overline{w}$ एक ऋणात्मक वास्तविक संख्या है, जहाँ $\overline{w}$, $w$ का संयुग्मी सम्मिश्र है। तब $l+m+n$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: $|3-4\mathrm{i}|=5$ and $3-4\mathrm{i}$ lies in the fourth quadrant, so $3-4\mathrm{i}=5e^{-\mathrm{i}\varphi}$ with $\varphi=\tan^{-1}\dfrac43\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\cos\varphi=\dfrac35$, $\sin\varphi=\dfrac45$.

Then $(3-4\mathrm{i})\overline{w}=3e^{-\mathrm{i}(\theta+\varphi)}$. This is a negative real number exactly when $\theta+\varphi$ is an odd multiple of $\pi$, so $\theta=\pi-\varphi$ up to multiples of $2\pi$.
Since $\hat{u}$ is a unit vector, $l^2+m^2+n^2=1$, and $l^2+m^2=|w|^2=\dfrac{9}{25}$, so $n^2=\dfrac{16}{25}$.
The angle with the positive $z$-axis is obtuse, so $n=\cos\gamma<0$, that is $n=-\dfrac45=-0.8$.
originality_note: New: the first two direction cosines of a unit vector are packed into a complex number w = l + i m, and w is fixed by its modulus and by a conjugate-argument condition ((3-4i) times conj(w) negative real); the third direction cosine then comes from l^2+m^2+n^2 = 1 with |w|^2 = l^2+m^2 (way 5, link of two chapters). Closest known: 'find z with arg((3-4i) z) = pi' or 'direction cosines from two given ones'. Different because: the modulus of w is the sine of the angle with the z-axis, so the two chapters meet in one identity.

concept_use.Basic properties of a vector: Unit vector: l^2+m^2+n^2 = 1 gives n^2 = 1 - |w|^2, and the obtuse angle with the z-axis fixes the sign of the direction cosine n.
concept_use.Conjugate, modulus and argument of a com: Conjugate turns arg into -theta; (3-4i) conj(w) negative real forces arg w = pi - tan^-1(4/3); modulus |w| = 3/5 then gives l and m.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, vector and point is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Wrote the imaginary unit as an upright i and defined it, so it is not confused with the unit vector i-hat; defined the conjugate bar; stated the obtuse angle with the positive z-axis to fix the sign of n. Changed: used \mathrm{i} for the imaginary unit.
key_step: Turning '(3-4i) conj(w) is negative real' into arg w = pi - tan^-1(4/3), then n from the unit-vector condition.
justification: Two standard results chained (argument of a product with a conjugate, direction cosine identity) plus a sign decision; routine but multi-step, like 2025-P2-Q1 (L2) and 2026-P2-Q1 (L2).
